title: Largest nearby events showed no clear early rank on days 1-30 after 58 shallow M7 to below 8 earthquakes in 2001-2024
abstract: We tested whether the largest nearby earthquake occurs early in event order after the first day. A fixed USGS ComCat snapshot gave 58 sequences with 237 shallow M5.5 or larger neighbors on days 1 to before 30 after isolated shallow M7 to below 8 centers in 2001-2024. Each neighbor was assigned once. We gave each sequence equal weight and kept magnitude ties. The mean order score was 0.486, versus 0.5 under exchangeable magnitude labels. The two-sided conditional shuffle p value was 0.788. The 95% spatial bootstrap interval was 0.407 to 0.567, and the three-year block interval was 0.375 to 0.600. Planned changes in radius, time window, magnitude floor, magnitude type and center isolation also gave no clear shuffle result. A hypothetical power check showed low power for small early shifts. The result does not prove independence, identify caused aftershocks or give a hazard forecast. Selection, detection, magnitude mixtures, sparse sequences and dependence limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, saved draws, source hashes, retrieval instructions, an independent assignment audit and a figure are included. External catalog records stay outside the package.

display.caption: Largest-event order score in the primary sample and planned checks. An early rank has a score near zero. A late rank has a score near one. The conditional null mean is 0.5. Left: conditional shuffle draws and observed mean. Right: spatial bootstrap intervals. These intervals do not model all sequence dependence.
